newsitem.title: USA: Forensics expert to review JonBenet autopsy photos.
newsitem.headline: Forensics expert to review JonBenet autopsy photos.

text.p: A forensics expert who played a key role in the O.J. Simpson murder trial said on Friday he would review autopsy photos and other documents in the murder investigation of 6-year-old JonBenet Ramsey.

But Dr. Henry Lee, director of the Connecticut State Police forensics laboratory, told a news conference there were no plans to send physical evidence, such as hair, blood or DNA samples, to his office in Connecticut.
He said he would reconstruct the crime scene based on information he received from Colorado police. "One photograph can tell the whole story sometimes," he said.
Lee and DNA expert Barry Scheck officially joined the investigation into the murder of the young beauty pageant winner on Thursday, at the invitation of Colorado prosecutors.

The criminologist testified for the defence in the Simpson criminal trial and gave a taped deposition on behalf of the defence in the civil trial. Scheck also assisted the defence in Simpson's criminal trial.
Lee said he met on Thursday evening with Boulder police officials, but added he had no plans to go to Colorado and had not been requested to do so.

Lee, who urged reporters to stop calling him about the case, said there was no time frame or deadline for his investigation. "This will be the first and last news conference in regards to this case," he added.
He said he would testify in court if called upon. "Our mission is to report scientific fact," he said.
Ramsey's body was found on Dec. 26 by her father in a windowless basement room of the family's Boulder home about eight hours after her mother said she found a ransom note demanding $118,000.
No suspects have been named in the seven-week murder probe.
